newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks close just firm, off highs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks close just firm, off highs.

text.p: 10yrbond futs cl 92.595 +0.130 Gold NY 354.35 Lon fix 353.40
*Stocks ended just up, mostly ignoring the Dow's rise after a Greenspan speech on Tuesday. Volume 467.1 million, value A$835.7 million, 1,111 stocks traded, 350 steady, 378 up, 383 down

Australian shares finished a touch higher with investors mostly ignoring the solid performance from the Dow after an address to a U.S. senate committee by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan failed to deter U.S. markets.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index finished 3.2 points up at 2,433.5, ten points off its intra-day high of 2,443.5.
The March share price index closed two points firmer at 2,438, a slim 4.5 point premium to the underlying index.
The market got off to a reasonable start but failed to follow through and started to drift after lunch as buying for bellwether issue BHP gradually evaporated.

"Investors are still worried about BHP which has lagged the market since the middle of last year - they are waiting to see more concrete signs of a recovery for the big Australian," a Brisbane-based dealer said.
Another negative factor was the S&P 500 March futures contract which drifted into negative territory late in our session, the dealer said.
He said the market would likely have finished lower on the day except for some late buying interest in major bank issues which had trailed the market for most of the session.

The gold sector saw the most excitement on the day with big turnover and a hefty rise in Mt Edon Gold Mines stock during the day. A joint takeover for the company by Camelot Resources and Canadian group Teck Corp was announced after the close of trade.
However, Papua New Guinean gold miner Goldfields slipped after announcing a further earnings downgrade.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Derivative trade was subdued with options turnover subsiding after some big trade in bank related call options on Tuesday.
Total options traded 28,310 (66,016).
Turnover in March SPI contracts 6,741 (5,419).

In other markets, Australian bonds held onto gains made in after hours SYCOM trade but failed an attempted break through resistance early on and spent the rest of the session consolidating above support in quiet trade.

The yield on 10-year T-bonds closed at 7.32 percent, 0.13 percentage points below Tuesday's close. The Australian dollar was slightly weaker after spending a quiet session trapped in a narrow range as market focus remained on its U.S. counterpart.
At 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), the local dollar was quoted at US$0.7767/72.
Short-term range Support Restnce RSI-14 MA-10 MA-20
